blocks.content: A grain merchant claims to sell at the cost price of ₹{costPricePerTrueQuantity} for {trueQuantity} kg, but his scale delivers only {deliveredQuantity} kg.

stem.prompt: What is his actual profit percentage?

explanation.opening: The merchant receives payment for the full quantity but bears the cost of only the quantity actually delivered.
explanation.concept: Actual profit must be compared with the cost of the delivered goods, not with the cost of the billed quantity.

steps.title: Find the cost of the delivered grain
steps.body: Scale the true cost in the ratio delivered quantity to true quantity.

steps.title: Compare payment with delivered cost
steps.body: At stated cost price, the amount charged is C. Calculate profit on C_d.

explanation.conclusion: This rate is the merchant's actual profit from the short weight.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not divide profit by the amount charged; profit percentage is based on the merchant's actual cost.

PNL-QL-121.difficultyRationale: One visible quantity adjustment followed by a direct profit-rate calculation.

blocks.content: A shopkeeper's true cost for {trueQuantity} kg of packaged rice is ₹{costPricePerTrueQuantity}. He charges ₹{quotedSellingPricePerNominalQuantity} for the pack but supplies only {deliveredQuantity} kg.

stem.prompt: Find the actual profit or loss amount and percentage.

explanation.opening: Let us separate the billed amount from the cost of the quantity actually supplied.
explanation.concept: The selling amount is quoted for the nominal pack, while actual cost depends on delivered quantity.

steps.title: Calculate delivered cost
steps.body: Use proportional cost for {deliveredQuantity} out of {trueQuantity} units.

steps.title: Find the amount result
steps.body: Subtract delivered cost from the charged amount.

steps.title: Convert to a percentage
steps.body: Measure the amount on C_d.

explanation.conclusion: The sign of A gives profit or loss, and the ratio gives the percentage.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not use the cost of the full nominal quantity after the seller has supplied less.

PNL-QL-122.difficultyRationale: Proportional cost, amount result, and percentage interpretation.

blocks.content: A fruit seller declares a {declaredRatePercent}% {declaredDirection} on fruit costing ₹{costPricePerTrueQuantity} per {trueQuantity} kg, but supplies only {deliveredQuantity} kg for each billed lot.

stem.prompt: Calculate the actual percentage gain or loss.

explanation.opening: The declared rate determines the billed price, while the short delivery changes the seller's actual cost.
explanation.concept: Combine the price multiplier with the delivered-quantity ratio before measuring the true result.

steps.title: Find the quoted selling amount
steps.body: Apply the declared profit or loss factor to the true cost of the nominal quantity.

steps.title: Find actual delivered cost
steps.body: Scale cost by d/q.

steps.title: Calculate the actual rate
steps.body: Compare S with C_d.

explanation.conclusion: This gives the genuine result after both price declaration and short delivery.
explanation.commonTrap: The declared rate is not the actual rate because the quantity base has also changed.

PNL-QL-123.difficultyRationale: Direct combination of one price factor and one quantity factor.

blocks.content: Cooking oil costs ₹{costPricePerTrueQuantity} per {trueQuantity} litres. A retailer advertises a {declaredRatePercent}% {declaredDirection} but dispenses only {deliveredQuantity} litres for the billed quantity.

stem.prompt: Find the retailer's actual profit or loss percentage.

explanation.opening: A declared loss can still become an actual profit when the delivered quantity is short.
explanation.concept: Price and quantity changes must be combined on the same actual-cost basis.

steps.title: Turn the declared rate into a price
steps.body: Apply the stated commercial multiplier to the nominal cost.

steps.title: Find the cost of oil actually delivered
steps.body: Use the delivered-to-true quantity ratio.

steps.title: Compare the two amounts
steps.body: Measure the difference between billed price and C_d on C_d.

explanation.conclusion: The comparison reveals the actual direction and rate.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not assume that a declared loss guarantees an actual loss when quantity is manipulated.

PNL-QL-124.difficultyRationale: Hidden actual-cost base but a direct forward calculation.

blocks.content: Fertilizer costs ₹{costPricePerTrueQuantity} for {trueQuantity} kg and is billed at ₹{quotedSellingPricePerNominalQuantity} per bag.

stem.prompt: How much fertilizer should each bag contain to produce an actual {targetRatePercent}% {targetDirection}?

explanation.opening: This time the target result is known and the delivered quantity is the unknown.
explanation.concept: The cost of the delivered quantity must equal the billed amount divided by the target commercial multiplier.

steps.title: Find the allowable delivered cost
steps.body: Reverse the target profit or loss factor from the quoted selling amount.

steps.title: Convert cost to quantity
steps.body: Use proportional cost per unit of true quantity.

explanation.conclusion: The resulting quantity is the amount that must be delivered per billed bag.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not apply the target rate directly to quantity; first recover the allowable cost.

PNL-QL-125.difficultyRationale: Inverse target-rate problem with quantity as the unknown.

blocks.content: The cost of {trueQuantity} fasteners is ₹{costPricePerTrueQuantity}. A seller supplies only {deliveredQuantity} fasteners in each nominal pack.

stem.prompt: What price should be charged to obtain an actual {targetRatePercent}% {targetDirection}?

explanation.opening: The selling price must be based on the cost of the reduced pack, not the nominal pack.
explanation.concept: Find actual delivered cost first, then apply the target commercial multiplier.

steps.title: Find cost of the supplied fasteners
steps.body: Scale the nominal cost by delivered quantity divided by true quantity.

steps.title: Apply the target rate
steps.body: Multiply C_d by the appropriate profit or loss factor.

explanation.conclusion: This is the required quoted price for the short pack.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not apply the target rate to the full-quantity cost.

PNL-QL-126.difficultyRationale: Direct quantity adjustment followed by one target-rate multiplier.

blocks.content: A sugar trader pays ₹{purchasePricePerNominalQuantity} for a nominal {nominalQuantity} kg but receives {receivedQuantity} kg. He later charges ₹{sellingPricePerNominalQuantity} for each nominal lot while delivering only {deliveredQuantity} kg.

stem.prompt: Find his actual profit percentage.

explanation.opening: The trader gains on both sides: extra quantity while buying and short quantity while selling.
explanation.concept: Compute the real cost per received unit and the real revenue per delivered unit on a common quantity basis.

steps.title: Find actual unit cost
steps.body: Spread the purchase payment over the quantity actually received.

steps.title: Find revenue per delivered unit
steps.body: Spread the billed sale amount over the quantity actually supplied.

steps.title: Compare unit values
steps.body: Measure profit on actual unit cost.

explanation.conclusion: This rate captures both the heavy buying measure and the light selling measure.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not compare the two nominal prices without adjusting for received and delivered quantities.

PNL-QL-127.difficultyRationale: Dual-side quantity deception with two normalized unit values.

blocks.content: An oil dealer pays ₹{purchasePricePerNominalQuantity} for a nominal {nominalQuantity}-litre purchase but receives {receivedQuantity} litres. He charges ₹{sellingPricePerNominalQuantity} per nominal sale and supplies {deliveredQuantity} litres.

stem.prompt: Calculate the actual percentage gain or loss.

explanation.opening: We should remove the misleading nominal quantities and compare true per-litre values.
explanation.concept: Actual result depends on money per unit received and money per unit delivered.

steps.title: Normalize purchase cost
steps.body: Divide purchase payment by actual received quantity.

steps.title: Normalize selling realization
steps.body: Divide selling charge by actual delivered quantity.

steps.title: Calculate the percentage result
steps.body: Compare normalized realization with normalized cost on the cost base.

explanation.conclusion: The sign and size of the unit-value difference give the actual result.
explanation.commonTrap: Nominal quantities are labels; the true physical quantities determine actual cost and realization.

blocks.content: Spices cost ₹{costPricePerTrueQuantity} per {trueQuantity} g. A retailer marks them {markupPercent}% above cost, allows {discountPercent}% discount, and supplies only {deliveredQuantity} g for each billed pack.

stem.prompt: Find the actual profit or loss percentage.

explanation.opening: Three effects are interacting here: markup, discount, and short delivery.
explanation.concept: Combine the price factors to get the billed amount, then compare it with the cost of the quantity actually supplied.

steps.title: Find the billed price
steps.body: Apply markup and discount successively.

steps.title: Find delivered cost
steps.body: Scale C by delivered quantity divided by true quantity.

steps.title: Calculate actual rate
steps.body: Compare S with delivered cost on the delivered-cost base.

explanation.conclusion: The resulting rate is the retailer's true profit or loss.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not calculate the discount on cost price or ignore the short quantity.

PNL-QL-129.difficultyRationale: Successive price transformations combined with quantity deception.

blocks.content: Paint costs ₹{costPricePerTrueQuantity} for {trueQuantity} litres. A dealer fills only {deliveredQuantity} litres, allows {discountPercent}% discount, and wants an actual {targetRatePercent}% {targetDirection}.

stem.prompt: By what percentage should the can be marked above cost?

explanation.opening: The unknown markup must compensate for both the discount and the reduced delivered cost.
explanation.concept: Set the discounted marked price equal to the target realization on actual delivered cost.

steps.title: Find actual delivered cost
steps.body: Scale nominal cost by d/q.

steps.title: Find target selling amount
steps.body: Apply the target multiplier to delivered cost.

steps.title: Reverse the discount to find marked price
steps.body: Divide target selling amount by the retained discount factor.

steps.title: Convert marked price to markup
steps.body: Compare marked price with nominal cost.

explanation.conclusion: The final comparison gives the required markup percentage.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not apply markup to delivered cost if the marked price is defined relative to the nominal cost price.

PNL-QL-130.difficultyRationale: Coupled inverse across quantity, discount, target result, and markup.

blocks.content: Cereal costs ₹{costPricePerTrueQuantity} per {trueQuantity} g and is marked {markupPercent}% above cost. Each packet contains only {deliveredQuantity} g.

stem.prompt: What discount should be allowed to obtain an actual {targetRatePercent}% {targetDirection}?

explanation.opening: We know the marked price and target result, so the discount can be isolated.
explanation.concept: Target selling amount is based on delivered cost; discount is measured from marked price.

steps.title: Calculate delivered cost
steps.body: Use the quantity ratio d/q.

steps.title: Find target selling amount
steps.body: Apply the required profit or loss factor to delivered cost.

steps.title: Find the retained fraction of marked price
steps.body: Divide target selling amount by marked price.

steps.title: Convert retained fraction to discount
steps.body: Discount% = 100% minus retained percentage.

explanation.conclusion: The shortfall from the marked price is the required discount.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not calculate target profit on the nominal full-quantity cost.

PNL-QL-131.difficultyRationale: Inverse discount with markup and short-delivery bases.

blocks.content: A cement dealer changes the quoted price by {priceChangePercent}% in the {priceDirection} direction on bags costing ₹{costPricePerTrueQuantity} for {trueQuantity} kg, and supplies {shortQuantityPercent}% less cement.

stem.prompt: Find the actual profit percentage.

explanation.opening: Both the price and the quantity have changed, so their factors should be combined.
explanation.concept: The billed-price factor affects revenue, while the retained-quantity factor affects actual cost.

steps.title: Write the price factor
steps.body: Use 1+p/100 for an increase or 1−p/100 for a decrease.

steps.title: Write the delivered-cost factor
steps.body: Supplying s% less means the cost factor is 1−s/100.

steps.title: Compare the factors
steps.body: Actual realization factor equals price factor divided by delivered-cost factor.

explanation.conclusion: The excess of this factor over 1 gives the actual profit percentage.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not subtract the short-quantity percentage from the price-change percentage.

PNL-QL-132.difficultyRationale: Direct interaction of one price factor and one quantity factor.

blocks.content: Animal feed costs ₹{costPricePerTrueQuantity} per {trueQuantity} kg. The seller changes the quoted price by {priceChangePercent}% in the {priceDirection} direction and short-delivers by {shortQuantityPercent}%.

stem.prompt: Calculate the actual percentage gain or loss.

explanation.opening: A price reduction can be offset by short delivery, so the final direction must be calculated rather than guessed.
explanation.concept: Compare the revenue multiplier with the cost multiplier of the delivered quantity.

steps.title: Form both multipliers
steps.body: Create the quoted-price factor and the delivered-quantity factor.

steps.title: Find the actual commercial factor
steps.body: Divide price factor by quantity factor.

steps.title: Interpret M
steps.body: M above 1 means gain; M below 1 means loss.

explanation.conclusion: The distance of M from 1 gives the actual rate.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not decide the direction from the price change alone.

PNL-QL-133.difficultyRationale: Direct factor comparison with a direction interpretation.

blocks.content: A customer pays for {trueQuantity} units of a product but receives only {deliveredQuantity} units.

stem.prompt: By what percentage is the effective price per true unit higher?

explanation.opening: The same payment is spread over fewer units, so the effective unit price rises.
explanation.concept: Effective overcharge is measured relative to the fair unit price.

steps.title: Form the price ratio
steps.body: Effective price per unit is nominal payment divided by delivered quantity, while fair price uses true quantity.

steps.title: Convert ratio to overcharge
steps.body: Subtract 1 from q/d and multiply by 100.

explanation.conclusion: This percentage is the customer's effective overcharge.
explanation.commonTrap: The overcharge percentage is not simply the percentage shortage unless the shortage is measured on the delivered quantity.

blocks.content: A dry-fruit seller declares a {declaredRatePercent}% {declaredDirection} while billing for {trueQuantity} g. He wants the actual result to be {actualRatePercent}% {actualDirection}.

stem.prompt: How much should each pack actually contain?

explanation.opening: The billed price comes from the declared rate, but the target actual rate determines the allowable delivered cost.
explanation.concept: Equate the same selling amount under the declared-price model and the target-actual-result model.

steps.title: Find billed selling amount
steps.body: Apply the declared multiplier to nominal cost.

steps.title: Recover allowable delivered cost
steps.body: Divide the selling amount by the actual target multiplier.

steps.title: Convert cost to quantity
steps.body: Use direct proportionality between cost and delivered quantity.

explanation.conclusion: The resulting quantity produces the requested actual rate.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not equate declared and actual percentages; they use different cost bases.

PNL-QL-135.difficultyRationale: Coupled inverse using declared and actual rates to solve quantity.

blocks.content: A seller charges for {trueQuantity} g of coffee but supplies {deliveredQuantity} g and earns an actual {actualRatePercent}% {actualDirection}.

stem.prompt: Find the declared profit or loss percentage on the price list.

explanation.opening: We know the true result after short delivery and must reconstruct the rate printed on the price list.
explanation.concept: Actual selling amount equals delivered cost multiplied by the actual-result factor; compare that amount with nominal cost to obtain the declared rate.

steps.title: Express delivered cost
steps.body: Use C_d=C(d/q).

steps.title: Find the selling amount
steps.body: Apply the actual multiplier to C_d.

steps.title: Compare with nominal cost
steps.body: The relative difference between selling amount and C gives the declared rate.

explanation.conclusion: This reconstructed rate is the declared profit or loss percentage.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not report the actual rate again; the price-list base is the full nominal cost.

PNL-QL-136.difficultyRationale: Reverse base conversion from actual result to declared rate.

blocks.content: A tea seller charges ₹{quotedSellingPricePerNominalQuantity} for {trueQuantity} g but supplies {deliveredQuantity} g. This gives an actual {actualRatePercent}% {actualDirection}.

stem.prompt: Find the true cost price per {trueQuantity} g.

explanation.opening: The quoted amount and actual rate first tell us the cost of the tea actually delivered.
explanation.concept: Reverse the actual commercial multiplier, then scale delivered cost up to the true nominal quantity.

steps.title: Recover delivered cost
steps.body: Divide the quoted selling amount by the actual result factor.

steps.title: Scale to nominal cost
steps.body: Multiply delivered cost by q/d.

explanation.conclusion: The scaled value is the true cost for the full nominal quantity.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not treat the quoted price as the cost of the full quantity before reversing the actual rate.

PNL-QL-137.difficultyRationale: Reverse actual-rate calculation followed by quantity rescaling.

blocks.content: A retailer charges ₹{quotedSellingPricePerNominalQuantity} for {trueQuantity} g of nuts, supplies {deliveredQuantity} g, and makes an actual {actualDirection} of ₹{actualAmount}.

stem.prompt: Find the true cost price per {trueQuantity} g.

explanation.opening: The actual amount result lets us recover the cost of the quantity supplied directly.
explanation.concept: Undo the profit or loss amount from the selling amount, then scale delivered cost to nominal quantity.

steps.title: Recover delivered cost
steps.body: For profit, subtract the amount from selling price; for loss, add it.

steps.title: Scale to full quantity
steps.body: Use C=C_d(q/d).

explanation.conclusion: The scaled cost is the true nominal cost price.
explanation.commonTrap: Apply the actual amount before scaling; otherwise the amount is placed on the wrong quantity base.

PNL-QL-138.difficultyRationale: Direction-sensitive amount reversal and quantity scaling.

blocks.content: A pulses trader pays ₹{purchasePricePerNominalQuantity} and receives {receivedQuantity} kg. He charges ₹{sellingPricePerNominalQuantity} for each nominal sale.

stem.prompt: How much should he deliver per sale to obtain an actual {targetRatePercent}% {targetDirection}?

explanation.opening: The purchase side fixes actual unit cost; the target rate then fixes allowable cost per sale.
explanation.concept: Normalize the buying deal first, then solve the selling quantity from the target selling factor.

steps.title: Find actual unit cost
steps.body: Divide purchase payment by received quantity.

steps.title: Find allowable cost per sale
steps.body: Reverse the target multiplier from the selling charge.

steps.title: Convert allowable cost to delivered quantity
steps.body: Divide allowable sale cost by actual unit cost.

explanation.conclusion: The resulting quantity is the required delivery per nominal sale.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not use the nominal purchase quantity when the trader actually received a different amount.

PNL-QL-139.difficultyRationale: Dual-side inverse with target rate and delivered quantity unknown.

blocks.content: A flour trader pays ₹{purchasePricePerNominalQuantity} for a purchase lot and charges ₹{sellingPricePerNominalQuantity} while delivering {deliveredQuantity} kg per sale.

stem.prompt: How much flour must he receive in the purchase lot to obtain an actual {targetRatePercent}% {targetDirection}?

explanation.opening: Here the selling side is known and the extra quantity received while buying is the unknown advantage.
explanation.concept: Use target profit to determine allowable cost per delivered sale, then infer the purchase quantity that creates that unit cost.

steps.title: Recover target cost of delivered quantity
steps.body: Divide sale revenue by the target result factor.

steps.title: Find required unit cost
steps.body: Divide that cost by delivered quantity.

steps.title: Solve received quantity
steps.body: Received quantity equals total purchase payment divided by required unit cost.

explanation.conclusion: This purchase quantity gives the requested actual result.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not solve using the billed sale quantity as though it were also the received purchase quantity.

PNL-QL-140.difficultyRationale: Reverse dual-measure problem with received quantity unknown.

blocks.content: A customer is charged ₹{quotedSellingPricePerNominalQuantity} for {trueQuantity} units but receives only {deliveredQuantity} units.

stem.prompt: Find the effective price per true {trueQuantity} units.

explanation.opening: The charge remains unchanged, but fewer units are supplied.
explanation.concept: First find price per delivered unit, then scale it to the true reference quantity.

steps.title: Find effective unit price
steps.body: Divide the quoted charge by delivered quantity.

steps.title: Scale to the true quantity
steps.body: Multiply effective unit price by {trueQuantity}.

explanation.conclusion: This is what the customer effectively pays for a true {trueQuantity}-unit quantity.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not report the original quoted amount; it applies to the falsely measured pack.

stem.prompt: Which scheme gives the higher profit percentage, and by how many percentage points?

explanation.opening: To compare the schemes fairly, calculate each actual profit rate on its own true cost base.
explanation.concept: Different combinations of price and quantity deception must be normalized before comparison.

steps.title: Evaluate Scheme A
steps.body: Find its actual revenue-to-cost factor and convert it to a percentage.

steps.title: Evaluate Scheme B
steps.body: Repeat the same calculation on the second scheme.

steps.title: Compare the rates
steps.body: Identify the larger rate and subtract the smaller rate from it.

explanation.conclusion: The higher normalized rate identifies the more profitable scheme.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not compare only the shortages or only the quoted price changes.

PNL-QL-142.difficultyRationale: Two complete dishonest-trade computations followed by comparison.

blocks.content: The cost of {trueQuantity} packaged items is ₹{costPricePerTrueQuantity}. A seller charges ₹{quotedSellingPricePerNominalQuantity} for {trueQuantity} items but places only {deliveredQuantity} items in the carton.

stem.prompt: Find the actual profit percentage.

explanation.opening: A false count works exactly like a false weight: cost follows the number of items actually supplied.
explanation.concept: Scale nominal cost to the delivered count and compare it with the amount charged.

steps.title: Find cost of supplied items
steps.body: Use C_d=C(d/q).

steps.title: Calculate actual profit rate
steps.body: Compare the charged amount with C_d on the C_d base.

explanation.conclusion: The result is the seller's true profit percentage.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not assume that count-based fraud needs a different percentage formula from weight-based fraud.

PNL-QL-143.difficultyRationale: Direct false-count variant of proportional delivered cost.

blocks.content: A cloth merchant charges for {trueQuantity} cm, but the measuring rod marked as one metre is only {deliveredQuantity} cm long.

stem.prompt: Find the percentage overcharge caused by the short measure.

explanation.opening: The buyer pays for the full marked length but receives a shorter physical length.
explanation.concept: Effective price rises in the inverse ratio of true length to delivered length.

steps.title: Form the effective-price factor
steps.body: Divide true billed length by actual delivered length.

steps.title: Convert to overcharge percentage
steps.body: Subtract 1 and multiply by 100.

explanation.conclusion: This is the customer's effective overcharge percentage.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not report the percentage length shortage as the overcharge percentage; their bases differ.

PNL-QL-144.difficultyRationale: One inverse length ratio and percentage conversion.

blocks.content: Two dealer schemes are summarized in the table.

stem.prompt: Identify the more profitable scheme and calculate the difference in actual profit percentages.

explanation.opening: Read each table row as a complete scheme rather than comparing isolated cells.
explanation.concept: Actual profit factor combines the row's price factor and quantity factor.

steps.title: Calculate the first row's actual factor
steps.body: Normalize its price condition by its delivered-cost condition.

steps.title: Calculate the second row's actual factor
steps.body: Use the same method so the comparison is fair.

steps.title: Compare percentage rates
steps.body: Subtract the smaller actual rate from the larger one.

explanation.conclusion: The row with the higher normalized rate is the more profitable scheme.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not select a row simply because it has the larger price increase or larger shortage.

PNL-QL-145.difficultyRationale: Real table interpretation plus two multi-factor calculations.

blocks.content: Goods cost ₹{costPricePerTrueQuantity} per {trueQuantity} units, are marked up {markupPercent}%, discounted {discountPercent}%, and only {deliveredQuantity} units are supplied.

stem.prompt: Find the actual profit percentage.

explanation.opening: Let us organise the caselet into price-side and quantity-side effects.
explanation.concept: Markup and discount create the billed price; short delivery determines actual cost.

steps.title: Calculate billed price
steps.body: Apply markup first and discount second.

steps.title: Calculate delivered cost
steps.body: Scale nominal cost by delivered quantity divided by true quantity.

steps.title: Measure actual profit
steps.body: Compare billed price with delivered cost on the delivered-cost base.

explanation.conclusion: The combined caselet effects give the actual profit percentage.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not treat the caselet's percentages as though they all use the same base.

PNL-QL-146.difficultyRationale: Caselet extraction with successive price changes and quantity fraud.

blocks.content: A dealer charges for {trueQuantity} units but supplies only {deliveredQuantity} units.

statements: The percentage shortage is always equal to the percentage overcharge.
The effective price factor is true quantity divided by delivered quantity.
Overcharge should be measured on the amount paid rather than the fair unit price.

stem.prompt: Select the correct statement.

explanation.opening: The statements can be checked by comparing fair and effective unit prices.
explanation.concept: With the same payment, effective unit price changes in the inverse ratio q/d.

steps.title: Write the effective factor
steps.body: Effective price divided by fair price equals q/d.

steps.title: Evaluate the statements
steps.body: Only the statement consistent with this factor is correct.

explanation.conclusion: Choose the statement that uses the inverse quantity ratio.
explanation.commonTrap: Shortage and overcharge percentages usually have different bases.

PNL-QL-147.difficultyRationale: Conceptual statement evaluation using one established ratio.

blocks.question: The false quantity required for an actual {targetRatePercent}% profit on a nominal {trueQuantity}-unit sale is to be determined.

stem.prompt: Decide whether either statement alone, both together, or neither is sufficient.

explanation.opening: We are testing whether the selling amount and true unit cost are known well enough to solve one quantity.
explanation.concept: Delivered quantity is unique only when the target factor and the ratio between selling amount and nominal cost are fixed.

steps.title: Test Statement I alone
steps.body: Check whether it fixes every value needed in d=qS/[C(1+r)].

steps.title: Test Statement II alone
steps.body: Repeat the completeness test without using Statement I.

steps.title: Combine if necessary
steps.body: Use both statements only after each has been judged independently.

explanation.conclusion: Select the data-sufficiency option matching when the quantity becomes unique.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not calculate a numerical quantity from both statements while deciding whether one statement alone is sufficient.

PNL-QL-148.difficultyRationale: Data-sufficiency analysis for an inverse quantity equation.

blocks.content: A dealer charges for {trueQuantityExpression} units, supplies {deliveredQuantityExpression} units, and earns an actual profit of {actualRatePercent}%.

stem.prompt: Determine the declared profit or loss percentage algebraically.

explanation.opening: We can express the quantity deception as a cost ratio and then move back to the declared price base.
explanation.concept: Actual rate uses delivered cost, whereas declared rate compares the same selling amount with nominal cost.

steps.title: Express delivered cost symbolically
steps.body: Multiply nominal cost by delivered quantity divided by true quantity.

steps.title: Use the actual-rate equation
steps.body: Find the selling amount as a multiple of delivered cost.

steps.title: Compare with nominal cost
steps.body: Simplify S/C−1 and convert it to a signed percentage.

explanation.conclusion: The simplified expression is the declared profit or loss rate.
explanation.commonTrap: Keep the two percentage bases separate throughout the algebra.

PNL-QL-149.difficultyRationale: Symbolic reverse base conversion with quantity expressions.
